page: Amazon Web Services c7i-flex.12xlarge is a compute-optimized server instance powered by the Nitro hypervisor. It features 48 vCPUs and 24 physical cores based on the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8488C processor running at 3.2 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 96.0 GB of DDR5 memory operating at 5 GHz, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 9 Gbps.

The underlying Intel Xeon processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for tile and int8 operations. These hardware-level accelerators assist with cryptographic tasks via AES and SHA_NI, as well as integer and bit manipulation. The processor architecture also features a 105 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache per core, facilitating efficient data handling for complex mathematical computations.

In benchmark testing, the c7i-flex.12xlarge demonstrates strong performance in memory bandwidth, achieving 4111.32 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 222.1 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. Multi-threaded operations are highly efficient, as evidenced by a Geekbench multi-core score of 19030.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 65056.32. For specialized workloads, the server achieves top-tier text generation speeds of 353.0 tokens/second on small LLM models, though performance scales down to an average of 3.46 tokens/second on large 70B models. Single-core stress-ng performance remains in the average tier at 2062.89.

The c7i-flex family offers a cost-effective alternative within the compute-optimized class by delivering high-density compute resources without the premium of fully dedicated non-flex instances. The absence of local storage requires reliance on network-attached storage, which is a key architectural tradeoff. This configuration is suited for compute-intensive workloads such as software compilation, static web serving, database operations, and moderate-scale language model inference.
